## Does the DR-learner close the gap on the causal forest with more signal?

In the main competing-risk study the DR-learners lose to the causal forest on
pseudo-values almost everywhere. Every scenario × event cell there has
SD(τ)/SD(noise) of at most 0.29 (`results_processing/thesis_figures/rel_eff_snr.R`).
This page is scenario `r params$scenario` (`r survival_scenario_params$description[params$scenario]`).
The check moves away from the baseline (ρ = 0.5, censoring on, n = 500) one
factor at a time: a larger X3 effect (`hte_mult`, more signal at
n = 500) and a larger n (more data at the baseline signal). 100 runs per cell.
Full design in `README.md`.

The four n = 500 cells of a run share W, X and U, so the `hte_mult` comparison
is paired. The n cells are not. Every arm targets RMTL and is scored against
`tau_RMTL1` / `tau_RMTL2`. The semi-oracle twins (`*_semi`) use their parent's
outcome models with the true propensity 0.5.

```{r data}
res_path <- if (nzchar(params$res_path)) {
  params$res_path
} else {
  file.path(dirname(here()), "results", "competing_risk_snr")
}
figdir <- if (nzchar(params$fig_dir)) {
  params$fig_dir
} else {
  file.path(dirname(here()), "results", "all_figures", "competing_risk_snr")
}
SCEN <- as.integer(params$scenario)
figdir <- file.path(figdir, paste0("scenario_", SCEN))
dir.create(figdir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

metrics <- readRDS(file.path(res_path, "snr_metrics.RDS")) %>%
  filter(scenario == SCEN)
ratios <- readRDS(file.path(res_path, "snr_ratios.RDS")) %>%
  filter(scenario == SCEN)
stopifnot(nrow(metrics) > 0)
population <- file.path(res_path, "snr_population.RDS")
population <- if (file.exists(population)) {
  readRDS(population) %>% filter(scenario == SCEN)
} else {
  NULL
}

CF_ARM <- "pseudo_cf_whole_oob"
# display order; each semi-oracle twin shares its parent's colour
ARMS <- c("pseudo_cf_whole_oob", "pseudo_dr_whole_oob",
          "pseudo_dr_whole_oob_semi", "rsf_dr_oob", "rsf_dr_oob_semi")
SEMI_PAIRS <- c(pseudo_dr_whole_oob = "pseudo_dr_whole_oob_semi",
                rsf_dr_oob = "rsf_dr_oob_semi")
ARM_BASE <- setNames(ARMS, ARMS)
ARM_BASE[SEMI_PAIRS] <- names(SEMI_PAIRS)
BASE_LABELS <- SURV_ARM_LABELS[c(CF_ARM, names(SEMI_PAIRS))]
ARM_LABELS <- c(BASE_LABELS,
                setNames(paste(BASE_LABELS[names(SEMI_PAIRS)], "(e = 0.5)"),
                         SEMI_PAIRS))[ARMS]
# named, so a figure without the CF keeps the DR arms' colours
ARM_COLOURS <- setNames(
  as.character(paletteer::paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe")[seq_along(BASE_LABELS)]),
  BASE_LABELS
)
PROPENSITY_LABELS <- c("Estimated", "True (0.5)")

# the design (README.md): the cells this scenario has (scenarios 1-2 have no
# HTE multiplier axis). Population SNR at rho = 0.5, Event 1 / Event 2, from
# snr_population.R; the n cells all sit at the baseline's SNR
HTE_LEVELS <- sort(unique(metrics$hte_mult))
N_LEVELS <- sort(unique(metrics$n))
snr_label <- function(m) {
  if (is.null(population)) return("")
  s <- population %>% filter(hte_mult == m)
  sprintf("\n%.2f / %.2f", s$snr[s$target == "Event 1"],
          s$snr[s$target == "Event 2"])
}

# both factors go on one numeric x, hte_mult at 1-4 and n at 11-14, so a
# single facet_grid() can show them side by side with free x and one y per row
X_BREAKS <- c(seq_along(HTE_LEVELS), 10 + seq_along(N_LEVELS))
X_LABELS <- c(paste0("×", HTE_LEVELS, vapply(HTE_LEVELS, snr_label, "")),
              format(N_LEVELS, big.mark = ","))
PANEL_LABELS <- c(
  hte = "More signal: HTE multiplier at n = 500\n(SNR Event 1 / Event 2)",
  n = "More data: n at HTE ×1"
)
Z <- qnorm(0.975)
```

```{r helpers}
#' Put each row on the panel(s) it belongs to. The baseline (n = 500,
#' hte_mult 1) is in both
on_axes <- function(df) {
  bind_rows(
    df %>%
      filter(n == 500) %>%
      mutate(panel = "hte", pos = match(hte_mult, HTE_LEVELS)),
    df %>%
      filter(hte_mult == 1) %>%
      mutate(panel = "n", pos = 10 + match(n, N_LEVELS))
  ) %>%
    mutate(panel = factor(PANEL_LABELS[panel], levels = PANEL_LABELS))
}

#' The arm's colour group, propensity and dodged x
add_arm <- function(df, arms) {
  k <- length(arms)
  df %>%
    mutate(
      arm = factor(ARM_LABELS[framework], levels = ARM_LABELS[arms]),
      base = factor(BASE_LABELS[ARM_BASE[framework]], levels = BASE_LABELS),
      propensity = factor(
        if_else(framework %in% SEMI_PAIRS, PROPENSITY_LABELS[2],
                PROPENSITY_LABELS[1]),
        levels = PROPENSITY_LABELS
      ),
      x = pos + (match(framework, arms) - (k + 1) / 2) * 0.7 / k
    )
}

#' Estimate +/- interval per arm and cell, the hte_mult and n panels side by
#' side, a row per event
#'
#' @param est n, hte_mult, target, framework, est, lo, hi
#' @param runs optional n, hte_mult, target, framework, value: per-run points
#'   drawn faintly behind the estimates
#' @param yref a dashed reference line, NA for none
snr_plot <- function(est, ylab, title, runs = NULL, yref = NA, log_y = FALSE) {
  arms <- intersect(ARMS, unique(est$framework))
  est <- est %>% on_axes() %>% add_arm(arms)
  p <- ggplot(est, aes(x, est, colour = base, shape = propensity,
                       linetype = propensity, group = arm))
  if (!is.na(yref)) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = yref, linetype = "dashed",
                        colour = "grey50")
  }
  if (!is.null(runs)) {
    set.seed(1)
    runs <- runs %>%
      on_axes() %>%
      add_arm(arms) %>%
      mutate(x = x + runif(n(), -0.3, 0.3) * 0.7 / length(arms))
    p <- p + geom_point(data = runs, aes(y = value), shape = 16, size = 0.4,
                        alpha = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE)
  }
  p <- p +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = 0.6,
                   linetype = "solid") +
    geom_point(size = 2, fill = "white", stroke = 0.8) +
    facet_grid(target ~ panel, scales = "free", space = "free_x") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = X_BREAKS, labels = X_LABELS,
                       expand = expansion(add = 0.4)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = ARM_COLOURS) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = setNames(c(16, 21), PROPENSITY_LABELS)) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(c("solid", "dashed"),
                                            PROPENSITY_LABELS)) +
    drf_theme() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical",
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = ylab, colour = "Arm",
         shape = "Propensity", linetype = "Propensity")
  if (log_y) p <- p + scale_y_log10()
  # the paired differences carry production arms only
  if (all(est$propensity == PROPENSITY_LABELS[1])) {
    p <- p + guides(shape = "none", linetype = "none")
  }
  p
}

#' Mean +/- 95% CI (mean +/- z x MCSE) of one metric, per arm and cell
metric_est <- function(df, col) {
  df %>%
    group_by(n, hte_mult, target, framework) %>%
    summarise(
      est = mean(.data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE),
      mcse = sd(.data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(.data[[col]]))),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(lo = est - Z * mcse, hi = est + Z * mcse)
}

#' One tab per spec, written from a results="asis" chunk. A spec is a list of
#' tab, plot and optionally save (a file name in figdir)
plot_tabs <- function(specs) {
  cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
  for (s in specs) {
    # knitr drops the newlines after a printed plot, so each cat() leads with
    # blank lines or the next heading glues onto the image
    cat("\n\n##", s$tab, "\n\n")
    print(s$plot)
    if (!is.null(s$save)) {
      ggsave(s$save, plot = s$plot, path = figdir, height = 18, width = 28,
             units = "cm")
    }
  }
  cat("\n\n:::\n\n")
}

cell_order <- function(df) arrange(df, desc(n == 500), n, hte_mult)
```

## Results coverage

The expected count is 100 runs per cell and arm. README route C (no treated
unit left event-free at the horizon, so NA whole-sample pseudo-values) can cost
about one run in the ×3 cell.

```{r coverage}
coverage <- metrics %>%
  group_by(n, hte_mult, framework) %>%
  summarise(runs = n_distinct(run), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(framework = factor(ARM_LABELS[framework], levels = ARM_LABELS)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = framework, values_from = runs, names_sort = TRUE) %>%
  cell_order()
kable(coverage, col.names = c("n", "HTE ×", names(coverage)[-(1:2)]))
```

```{r na-table}
na_table <- metrics %>%
  group_by(n, hte_mult, target, framework) %>%
  summarise(runs_with_na = sum(n_na > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            total_na = sum(n_na, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(total_na > 0) %>%
  mutate(framework = ARM_LABELS[framework]) %>%
  cell_order()
if (nrow(na_table) > 0) {
  kable(na_table, col.names = c("n", "HTE ×", "Event", "Arm",
                                "Runs with an NA estimate", "Total NA estimates"))
} else {
  cat("No missing CATE estimates in any collected run.")
}
```

## RMSE ratio, DR / causal forest on PV

This is the comparison the study exists for. Each faint point is one run's
RMSE of a DR arm divided by the same run's RMSE of the causal forest on
pseudo-values (`rel_eff_snr.R`'s ratio). Below 1 (dashed), DR did better. The
larger point is the geometric mean, exp(mean log ratio), with a 95% CI from the
MCSE of the mean log ratio. The y axis is on a log scale.

```{r ratio-plot, fig.height=8}
run_ratios <- metrics %>%
  filter(framework != CF_ARM) %>%
  select(n, hte_mult, run, target, framework, rmse) %>%
  inner_join(
    metrics %>%
      filter(framework == CF_ARM) %>%
      select(n, hte_mult, run, target, rmse_cf = rmse),
    by = c("n", "hte_mult", "run", "target")
  ) %>%
  mutate(value = rmse / rmse_cf) %>%
  filter(is.finite(value), value > 0)

p_ratio <- snr_plot(
  ratios %>%
    mutate(est = geo_mean,
           lo = exp(log(geo_mean) - Z * mcse_log),
           hi = exp(log(geo_mean) + Z * mcse_log)),
  ylab = "RMSE ratio, DR / causal forest on PV",
  title = "DR-learners against the causal forest on PV",
  runs = run_ratios, yref = 1, log_y = TRUE
)
p_ratio
ggsave("snr_ratio.png", plot = p_ratio, path = figdir, height = 18,
       width = 28, units = "cm")
```

```{r ratio-table}
ratios %>%
  mutate(
    framework = ARM_LABELS[framework],
    median_iqr = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", median, q25, q75),
    geo_ci = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", geo_mean,
                     exp(log(geo_mean) - Z * mcse_log),
                     exp(log(geo_mean) + Z * mcse_log))
  ) %>%
  select(target, framework, n, hte_mult, runs, median_iqr, geo_ci,
         prop_dr_better) %>%
  arrange(target, factor(framework, levels = ARM_LABELS), desc(n == 500), n,
          hte_mult) %>%
  kable(digits = 2,
        col.names = c("Event", "Arm", "n", "HTE ×", "Runs",
                      "Median [IQR]", "Geometric mean (95% CI)",
                      "Share of runs DR better"))
```

## Absolute performance

Mean ± 95% CI (1.96 × MCSE) for every arm, the causal forest included. τ
itself grows with the HTE multiplier, so RMSE and bias are not comparable
across the left panel's columns. The ratio above is the like-for-like
comparison. Correlation and C-statistic are scale-free.

```{r abs-plots, results="asis", fig.height=8}
abs_specs <- list(
  list(tab = "RMSE", col = "rmse", ylab = "Mean RMSE",
       title = "RMSE of the CATE estimates", save = "snr_rmse.png"),
  list(tab = "Bias", col = "bias", ylab = "Mean bias", yref = 0,
       title = "Bias in the CATE estimates (estimate − truth)"),
  list(tab = "Correlation", col = "corr", ylab = "Mean correlation",
       title = "Correlation with the true CATE"),
  list(tab = "C-statistic", col = "c_stat", ylab = "Mean C-statistic",
       yref = 0.5, title = "C-statistic against the true CATE")
)
plot_tabs(lapply(abs_specs, function(s) {
  list(
    tab = s$tab, save = s$save,
    plot = snr_plot(metric_est(metrics, s$col), ylab = s$ylab,
                    title = s$title, yref = if (is.null(s$yref)) NA else s$yref)
  )
}))
```

## Cost of estimating the propensity

These are paired per-run differences, production arm minus its semi-oracle
twin, averaged with MCSE = sd(diff) / √pairs. A positive RMSE difference means
estimating the propensity costs accuracy. A positive C-statistic difference
means it helps.

```{r semi-plots, results="asis", fig.height=8}
paired_semi <- metrics %>%
  filter(framework %in% c(names(SEMI_PAIRS), SEMI_PAIRS)) %>%
  mutate(arm_type = if_else(framework %in% SEMI_PAIRS, "semi", "prod"),
         framework = ARM_BASE[framework]) %>%
  select(n, hte_mult, target, framework, run, arm_type, rmse, c_stat) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm_type, values_from = c(rmse, c_stat)) %>%
  mutate(rmse = rmse_prod - rmse_semi, c_stat = c_stat_prod - c_stat_semi)

plot_tabs(list(
  list(tab = "RMSE", save = "snr_semi_rmse.png",
       plot = snr_plot(metric_est(paired_semi, "rmse"),
                       ylab = "RMSE difference",
                       title = "Paired difference in RMSE, estimated − true propensity",
                       yref = 0)),
  list(tab = "C-statistic",
       plot = snr_plot(metric_est(paired_semi, "c_stat"),
                       ylab = "C-statistic difference",
                       title = "Paired difference in C-statistic, estimated − true propensity",
                       yref = 0))
))
```
